description:
The surah that opens with the oath of the Divine One swearing by every one of **The Stars**, as they descend and disappear beneath the horizon, that Muḥammad is indeed God's awaited Messenger. It takes its name from verse 1, which mentions "the stars" (najm). The surah confirms the divine source of the Prophet's message and refers to his ascension to heaven during the Night Journey (verse 1 ff.). The surah refutes the claims of the disbelievers about the goddesses and the angels (verse 19 ff.), and lists several truths about God's power. It closes with a warning of the imminent Day of Judgement.
The surah is also known as The Pleiades

2.1: That is, the Apostle of Allah.

6.2: That is, the Apostle of Allah (_ṣ_); or the Angel Gabriel, according to some commentators.

13.1: Or 'them.' To explain, the object of the pronoun _hū_ is specified in verse <{["Q", "53:18"]}>, 'Certainly he saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord.' This interpretation is also supported by a tradition of Imam ʿAli b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (_ʿa_) cited in the _Uṣūl al-Kāfī_, vol. 1, p. 95, _ḥadīth_ 2.

53.1: That is, Sodom. Elsewhere mentioned as plural; see <{["Q", "9:70"]}>, <{["Q", "69:9"]}>.

translations.1: By the star when it sets:<{["F", 1]}>
translations.2:
your companion<{["F", 1]}> has neither gone astray,
 nor gone amiss.
translations.3: Nor does he speak out of [his own] desire:
translations.4: it is just a revelation that is revealed [to him],
translations.5: taught him by One of great powers,
translations.6:
possessed of sound judgement.<{["F", 1]}>
 He<{["F", 2]}> settled,<{["F", 3]}>
translations.7: while he was on the highest horizon.
translations.8: Then he drew nearer and nearer
translations.9: until he was within two bows' length or even nearer,
translations.10:
whereat He revealed to His servant
   whatever He revealed.
translations.11: The heart did not deny what it saw.
translations.12: Will you then dispute with him about what he saw?!
translations.13: Certainly he saw it<{["F", 1]}> yet another time,
translations.14: by the Lote Tree of the Ultimate Boundary,
translations.15: near which is the Garden of the Abode,
translations.16: when there covered the Lote Tree what covered it.
translations.17:
The gaze did not swerve,
  nor did it overstep the bounds.
translations.18:
Certainly he saw
 some of the greatest signs of his Lord.
translations.19: Have you considered Lāt and ʿUzzā?
translations.21: Are you to have males and He females?
translations.22: That, then, will be an unfair division!
translations.23:
These are but names which you have coined
  —you and your fathers—
 for which Allah has not sent down any authority. They follow nothing but conjectures
  and the desires of the [lower] soul,
 while there has already come to them
  the guidance from their Lord.
translations.24: Shall man have whatever he yearns for?
translations.25: Yet to Allah belong this world and the Hereafter.
translations.26:
How many an angel there is in the heavens
   whose intercession is of no avail in any way
  except after Allah grants permission
   to whomever He wishes and approves of!
translations.27:
Indeed those who do not believe in the Hereafter
  give female names to the angels.
translations.28:
They do not have any knowledge of that.
 They follow nothing but conjectures,
 and indeed conjecture is no substitute for the truth.
translations.29:
So _avoid_ those who turn away from Our remembrance
  and desire nothing but the life of the world.
translations.30:
That is the ultimate reach of their knowledge.
 Indeed your Lord knows best
  those who stray from His way,
 and He knows best those who are [rightly] guided.
translations.31:
To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens
   and whatever is in the earth,
  that He may requite those who do evil
   for what they have done,
  and reward those who do good
   with the best [of rewards].
translations.32:
Those who avoid major sins
    and indecencies,
   excepting [minor and occasional] lapses. Indeed _your_ Lord is expansive in [His] forgiveness. He knows you best
 since [the time] He produced you from the earth,
 and since you were fetuses
  in the bellies of your mothers.
 So do not flaunt your piety:
  He knows best those who are Godwary.
translations.33: Did _you_ see him who turned away,
translations.34: gave a little and held off?
translations.35:
Does he have the knowledge of the Unseen
  so that he sees?
translations.36:
Has he not been informed of what is
  in the scriptures of Moses,
translations.37: and of Abraham, who fulfilled [his summons]:
translations.38: that no bearer shall bear another's burden,
translations.39:
and that nothing belongs to man
   except what he strives for,
translations.40: and that he will soon be shown his endeavour,
translations.41:
then he will be rewarded for it
    with the fullest reward;
translations.42: and that the terminus is toward _your_ Lord,
translations.43:
and that it is He who makes [men] laugh,
   and makes [them] weep,
translations.44: and that it is He who brings death and gives life,
translations.45:
and that it is He who created the mates,<{["F", 1]}>
   the male and the female,
translations.46: from a drop of [seminal] fluid when emitted;
translations.47: and that with Him lies the second genesis,
translations.48: and that it is He who enriches and grants possessions,
translations.49: and that it is He who is the Lord of Sirius;
translations.50: and that it is He who destroyed the former ʿĀd,
translations.52:
and the people of Noah before that;
 indeed they were more unjust and rebellious;
translations.53: and He overthrew the town that was overturned,<{["F", 1]}>
translations.54: covering it with what covered it.
translations.55:
Then which of the bounties of your Lord
  will you dispute?
translations.56:
This is a warner,
  [in the tradition] of the warners of old.
translations.57: The Imminent [Hour] is near at hand.
translations.58: There is none that may unveil it besides Allah.
translations.59: Do you then wonder at this discourse,
translations.62: So prostrate yourselves to Allah and worship Him!
